# Pure local qudit compression: direct dimension lower bound

Date: 2026-10-07. Status: internally derived proof, independently checked against a separate finite-grid proof by the quantum-statistics worker. No external correctness or priority claim. This result uses the exact finite-copy experiment and does not depend on an unverified Gaussian approximation. A later primary-source check found that the charged-total-dimension result follows from an established one-shot visible-compression converse. The stronger interface proved here concerns quantum branch dimension with unlimited classical outcomes; related Schmidt-number benchmark mechanisms are also established prior art, and novelty of the precise rate remains unestablished.

## Result and exact interface

Fix $q=d-1\ge1$ and $R>0$. The input is the unknown physical state

\[
 |\Phi_{n,z}\rangle
 =\left(\frac{|0\rangle+n^{-1/2}\sum_{a=1}^{q}z_a|a\rangle}
 {\sqrt{1+\|z\|^2/n}}\right)^{\otimes n},
 \qquad z\in\mathbb C^q,\quad\|z\|\le R.
\]

The encoder is a fixed CPTP map or quantum instrument, not a parameter-dependent preparation map. The decoder is a fixed channel, conditioned on the encoder's classical outcomes and any shared seed. There is no oracle revealing $z$, no input-dependent decoder side register outside the encoder, and no preshared encoder-decoder entanglement. The known inputs are $n,q,R$, the reference basis, and the model family. Channel computation is unrestricted; only retained memory dimension is optimized.

Write $Q$ for the largest quantum Hilbert-space dimension in any classical branch. Arbitrarily many classical measurement outcomes are permitted for the lower bound, even without charging them. In the originally requested charged hybrid interface, total dimension is $D=\sum_\ell\dim\mathcal M_\ell$, so $D\ge Q$. Independent public seeds are allowed.

The classical label register is dephased: coherence across distinct labels is quantum information and belongs to the quantum dimension. The branch bound does not declare a coherent direct sum to be free classical storage. The reconstruction criterion is

\[
 \sup_{\|z\|\le R}
 T\bigl(\Lambda_n(\Phi_{n,z}),\Phi_{n,z}\bigr)\le\epsilon,
 \qquad T(\rho,\sigma)=\tfrac12\|\rho-\sigma\|_1.
\]

# Bounded pure-state quantum compression: primary prior-art audit

Audit date: 7 October 2026. Scope: a single unknown coherent state in a full fixed-radius ball of `C^m`, or the whole local pure iid qudit state with `m=d-1`. Initially the resource is an arbitrary hybrid algebra `⊕_j M_{d_j}`, with **total dimension `D=Σ_j d_j`**. The later refinement charges **`Q=max_j d_j` with unlimited free dephased classical labels**. Reconstruction is worst-case trace distance. No external quantum side information or entanglement assistance. The local center, basis, radius, copy count and error target are supplied; the unknown amplitude is acquired only from the quantum input.

**Verdict:** the proposed `D = Θ((log(1/ε)/log log(1/ε))^m)` is mathematically credible under this interface, but its upper construction, unrestricted dimension converse, and classical obstruction are established mechanisms. The complete Θ law is an elementary synthesis of primary results, not a cleared frontier novelty. The stronger unlimited-classical `Q` statement is also credible and admits a direct proof, but its Stinespring and Schmidt-number mechanisms are explicit prior art. At most the fixed-radius quantitative synthesis and exact finite-copy uniform formulation remain uncleared. I did not find a paper explicitly advertising this ε→0 formula; that absence is weaker than novelty. Direct finite-copy arguments give symmetric-space saturation without a LAN error floor.

## Decisive primary results

1. **Hayashi (2002), _Exponents of quantum fixed-length pure-state source coding_, PRA 66, 032321.** [Latest arXiv v6](https://arxiv.org/html/quant-ph/0202002v6), Section V, proof of Lemma 4, Eqs. (30)–(32) and the subsequent inequality. For a pure-state ensemble with average `ρ`, an arbitrary **visible** encoder into a `D`-dimensional system and arbitrary CPTP decoder has average squared fidelity at most `Σ_{i≤D} λ_i(ρ)`. The proof uses a Stinespring dilation and Nielsen–Kempe majorization for a separable state. This is stronger than a unitary-decoder rank argument and stronger than the older loose `F<6Σ_{i≤D}λ_i` bound. Blind codes are a subset of visible codes. [Leditzky–Datta (2016), Lemma 5.2](https://arxiv.org/html/1407.6616v5#S5), restates exactly this spectral bound. I checked the original proof, not only the restatement.

# Quantum statistical experiments: rank-boundary Poisson–coherent experiment

7 October 2026. Scout: `quantum_statistics`. Source repository was read only.

## Executive assessment

The best new target in this branch is **compression of a bounded Poisson observation together with an unknown coherent state**. I obtain a written matching order law

\[
 D_{\rm opt}(\varepsilon)
 =\Theta_{\Lambda,R}\left[
 \left(\frac{\log(1/\varepsilon)}{\log\log(1/\varepsilon)}\right)^2\right],
 \tag{A}
\]

when **all classical and quantum retained dimensions are counted**. The maximal quantum branch dimension has only the first power, even if classical storage is free. The nonroutine step is showing that reconstruction for two unknown Poisson intensities forces preservation of low count labels; one may then apply the established visible pure-source spectral converse to a count × coherent ensemble. This is an internally derived theorem candidate with a complete argument below; priority and independent correctness review remain open.

There is a direct finite-copy quantum interface for (A). An unknown qubit with eigenvalue `lambda/n`, and unknown direction within `1/sqrt(n)` of a supplied pure reference, is uniformly equivalent in trace norm to

\[
 \operatorname{Pois}(\lambda)\otimes |z\rangle\langle z|,
 \qquad 0\le\lambda\le\Lambda,\quad |z|\le R,
 \tag{B}
\]

with bidirectional error `C_(Lambda,R)/n`. I give fixed channels and an elementary proof, including exact reverse composition. Existing work already recognizes near-pure Poisson behavior and spin Gaussian limits; the proposed increment is the explicit whole-experiment comparison and its uniform rate. This should not be advertised as discovering the two limit components.

The pure-state critical law is **not a major new theorem**: the photon cutoff and Hayashi visible-source converse already imply the polylogarithmic dimension order. Its exact finite-n saturation is useful to retain, but parent novelty review appropriately downgraded it. An independent expansion worker has derived an exact factorial excitation tail for the rare-mixed family, proving its required quantum dimension even below the comparison remainder. My audit of that factorial identity passed; see coordination notes below.
